sources.title: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly: October 2025 to Dec 2025
facts: The official-statistics release covers subsidy-attributable delivery from 1 October to 31 December 2025.
The release includes a bulletin, ODS tables, QMI and pre-release access record.
Quarterly delivery is distinct from monthly contract management information.
The publication includes revised figures from earlier periods.
Release-level metadata must be retained before trend comparison.

sources.title: Bulletin: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly October to December 2025
facts: The bulletin estimates 56,000 premises delivered during Q3 2025/26.
Cumulative gigabit-programme delivery was estimated at 1,373,800 premises.
GIS represented 75% of quarterly delivery, vouchers 18%, and Superfast plus Hubs 7%.
Historic delivery series are revised as supplier reporting improves.
Regional and residential-commercial aggregates do not establish parcel service.

sources.title: Quality and methodology information for BDUK delivery performance, quarterly
facts: Voucher UPRN validation uses expected premises passed and a 5% attrition adjustment.
A multiplier method with an 18% attrition adjustment is used where data quality is insufficient.
The multiplier-estimated share was 31% in the referenced quarterly release.
GIS reporting excludes premises where evidence shows prior overbuild by another supplier.
Method proportions can shift when project data are updated.

sources.title: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly: April 2025 to September 2025
facts: The official release covers subsidy-attributable delivery from April through September 2025.
The release contains bulletin, tables, QMI and pre-release access documents.
Earlier time periods may be revised in the release.
Official-statistics concepts must remain separate from management snapshots.
Publication and observation periods are distinct metadata fields.

sources.title: Bulletin: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly April to September 2025
facts: The bulletin covers two quarters between 1 April and 30 September 2025.
The workflow was changed to support shorter reporting lag.
The following update was intended to cover one new quarter plus cumulative totals.
Reported values are subsidy-attributable delivery statistics.
Cross-release comparison requires revision-aware time-series handling.

sources.title: Direct to Device licence exemption regulations update
facts: Ofcom made amended Direct-to-Device exemption regulations in June 2026.
The amendment covers specified frequencies in the 900 MHz band.
The regulations were intended to come into effect on 10 July 2026.
The framework supports MNO and satellite-operator partnerships.
Regulatory authorisation is not evidence of live service at a property.

sources.title: Mobile and wireless broadband below 5 GHz: D2D licence variation notice
facts: Ofcom approved a VodafoneThree licence variation on 10 April 2026.
The variation supports D2D satellite connectivity in paired 900 MHz frequencies.
Operation depended on the relevant exemption regulations entering force.
The authorisation covers UK territory and territorial waters under specified parameters.
A licence variation is not measured coverage or consumer availability.

sources.title: GigaHubs Process Review
facts: The process review evaluates GigaHubs delivery between 2021 and 2026.
The product connects remote public buildings such as schools, GP surgeries and libraries.
The evaluation uses management data and stakeholder interviews.
Hub connections are intended to support wider network effects around anchor sites.
Potential spillovers are evaluation hypotheses rather than parcel-level proof.

sources.title: GigaHubs Process Review Summary
facts: GigaHubs delivered approximately 1,200 Hub connections during 2021-26.
The review references 5,670 BDUK Hubs delivered as of September 2025.
Six projects were included in the programme review.
The evidence includes BDUK management information and qualitative interviews.
A connected public building does not automatically prove nearby household service.
